title: Rubik's Cube as a single-player game definition
description:
Define a 3x3 Rubik's Cube as a Baize game. Validates that the engine supports single-player puzzles, non-standard zone topologies, and complex perturber-driven state mutations.

## Why this matters
- Proves the engine handles single-player games
- Proves perturber language can express complex multi-piece coordinated mutations (face rotations)
- Proves CEL can express puzzle completion (all faces uniform color)
- Stress-tests the notation adapter with standard cube notation (U R F D L B)
- A solved cube is a satisfying demo

## Architecture
- 1 player: solver
- 6 grid zones (3x3 each): up, down, front, back, left, right
- 54 components: colored face stickers (9 per face, 6 colors)
- Moves: 12 basic (6 faces x CW/CCW) + 6 double moves = 18 total
- Each move is a perturber sequence of 20 swaps (8 stickers on the rotated face + 12 stickers on adjacent face edges)
- End condition: each face has all 9 stickers of the same color
- Notation: standard Singmaster (U, R, F, D, L, B, U', R2, etc.)

## Open questions
- Do we need a new zone topology for face adjacency, or can 6 independent grids + perturber handle it?
- Should center stickers be immovable (they define the face color)?
- How to represent scramble as initial setup?
close_reason: Already implemented. 25 Rust tests pass. 6-zone face topology, perturber rotations, solved-state CEL, scramble generation all done. Only remaining sub-issue is Singmaster notation (baize-wt9), blocked on notation adapter.
